name: AOWF — Day 1

date.source: Undated in the source; the file's own modification date is November 1999.

matches.note: One fall, sixty-minute time limit. Styx's own ringside interference (grabbing the mic, taunting the announcers) broke up the match's own flow shortly before the finish; Windsong hit the Graceful Flow and won via referee stoppage after Bright Light stopped answering a rope-break count.

notes: The alliance's own opening broadcast: four announcers introduce themselves as the sitting announcers of four separate member federations (Internet Championship Wrestling League, World Championship Internet Wrestling Association, a since-closed Ultimate Wrestling Federation, and World Wrestling Fantasy League). Opens with Savage Windsong (WCIWA) defeating Bright Light (ICWL) via referee stoppage after Styx's own ringside interference. Commentary previews a next match (the UWF's Jailbird vs. the WCIWA's Death) that the served text cuts off before reaching ("Click Here to continue on with the next matches") — neither wrestler's outcome nor any further detail is held. Day 2's own broadcast separately confirms an AOWF World Tag Team Championship was decided "last night" (i.e. on this Day 1 card), but no participant, team, or result for that match survives anywhere in the held text — gap-registered, not inferred; a prior pass's claim naming specific tag-team winners here was found unsupported by the served document and has been removed (see CURATION.md's own extraction-by-reading discipline).

name: AOWF — Day 2 (Television Championship unification)

date.source: Undated in the source; the file's own modification date is November 1999.

matches.note: Billed by Scott as "the Television 4 way": each of four member feds' own reigning Television Champion (WWFL's Blade, WCIWA's V.I.G., ICWL's The Charm, UWF's Golden One) sent to a backstage "back lot" to find four hidden AOWF TV Title replica plates; first to find all four and present them to the referee wins. The served text cuts off mid-brawl ("Day 2 concludes...") with The Charm having just chair-shotted V.I.G. — no winner is shown. Day 4's own broadcast later states three titles (TV, IC, Tag) were already crowned by that point, confirming a result exists, but the held record never names who won — gap-registered, not inferred.

notes: Guest interview: Ben interviews former WCIWA World Champion Richard Hope, who offers guidance to Stone ("current leader of the Masters of Armageddon") and distances himself from Styx specifically rather than the M.o.A.'s own membership. Main event: the AOWF Television Championship unification 4-way (see matches[]) — unresolved in the held text. A member wrestler (Eskridge, named only in passing by commentary) is referenced but does not appear. DISCLOSURE CORRECTION: this page's own provenance line previously claimed redactions while carrying zero redaction markers in its served text — a genuine miss, not a stale-but-accurate count. One real name — a special guest ringside announcer introduced as one of the AOWF's own founders, in a construction identical to the founders' names already redacted on Day 4 — was served unredacted and has now been redacted to match; see /curation.html. The page now discloses one redaction.

name: AOWF — Day 4 (World Championship, finale)

date.source: Undated in the source; the file's own modification date is November 1999.

matches.note: The AOWF World Heavyweight Championship's own founding match: a scored four-way (first to three falls wins, running score announced after every fall), not an elimination match — all four men stayed in throughout. Savage Warrior was counted out of the ring at one point; the referee ruled the fall to Nightshade ("since Nightshade was the only man in the ring, he is the only man who receives the fall") without eliminating Warrior, who continued competing and scored two falls of his own. Final score: Shame 2, Nightshade 3, Savage Warrior 2, Chaos 2 — Nightshade reached three falls first, the third a rollup on Shame while Warrior was still recovering, and was crowned champion.

notes: The finale of the alliance's first event, closing on the alliance's own founders (names redacted, per the privacy rule) presenting the belt to Nightshade — introduced by his new manager Dot, formerly associated with Flesh and the M.o.A. Ice and Blade assist the exhausted new champion to his feet afterward. This page carries eight redactions (real names, an out-of-fiction credit and a special-guest-referee introduction, both read aloud in-broadcast, per the privacy rule) — see /curation.html.

name: AOWF_2 — Day 1

date.source: Undated in the source; the alliance's own second event, run after AOWF_1 (November 1999).

matches.note: King of Extreme Tournament, seventh seed. Win by burying an opponent in a casket. Jon Clark helped the Minister of Violence bury Preacher, then abandoned the tournament outright rather than continue; the Minister dug Preacher back out afterward.

King of Extreme Tournament, sixth seed. Win by pinfall, submission, or throwing an opponent through one of the glass planes surrounding the ring. Fletcher Moran (billed "representing the PWA") eliminated by Donegan; Creed (billed "representing the PWA") won by finally shattering the plane under Donegan.

King of Extreme Tournament seed unspecified. Staged on location in a mocked-up school house; win by first pinfall. Grandel billed of the AWF this same night (see his own Scaffold Match below); Gregory billed "of Blue Chips Inc."; Blood billed "representing the GWIWC." Blood won with a second German suplex.

eliminations.note: Whipped by Mayhem into the interloping Abunai; both fell from the scaffold together.

matches.note: King of Extreme Tournament, eighth seed / Round 1 finale. Win by knocking an opponent off the scaffold and through the tables beneath. Abunai, an uninvited interloper never formally introduced as an entrant, physically climbs into the match mid-way and is present for Grandel's own elimination — recorded here as a fourth side since he actively wrestled within the match, not merely observed it. Santee wins with an Icebreaker that sends Mayhem from the scaffold.

For the AOWF Television Championship, declared vacant this same broadcast along with every other AOWF title (Ben, on-air: "all the titles have been declared vacant, and are to be decided through each of the four nights of this great event"). Retrieve the belt hanging above the ring via ladder. Hazzard's own knee was injured mid-match; Lana Jones's own interference (a spinning heel kick on Amanda) sent the contested belt into the crowd, where Riley reached it first and won. Referenced this title: aowf-television.

notes: The alliance's own second event: reopens on a memorial to William Riley AKA Flesh (per this wing's own confirmed identity, flesh-moa) and confirms the AOWF now includes PWA, AWF, and JWA as further member federations. Presents the AOWF's own 1999 awards show in three rounds across the broadcast (see awards.json for the full ledger) alongside the King of Extreme Tournament's own Round 1 (four matches) and the AOWF Television Championship's own Ladder Match. Styx makes a cameo accepting the Comeback of the Year award (see styx-moa's own aowf tenure). This page carries 2 redactions (real names), per the privacy rule — see /curation.html.
